title: Deep Learning Basics: How Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) Process Images

cues.en: -: Hello, and welcome back to the course on Deep Learning.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎回到深度學習課程。

cues.en: So we've learned quite a lot in this section of the course, let's summarize what we've talked about.
cues.zh: 這個章節學了不少，現在總結一下。

cues.en: All right, so here we go.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: We started with an input image, to which we applied multiple different feature detectors, or also called filters, to create these feature maps, and this comprises our convolutional layer.
cues.zh: 從輸入影像開始，套用多個不同的特徵偵測器，也就是濾波器，產生這些特徵圖，構成卷積層。

cues.en: Then, on top of that convolutional layer, we applied the ReLU, or Reified Linear Unit, to remove any linearity or increase non-linearity in our images.
cues.zh: 再對卷積層套用 ReLU，也就是修正線性單元，去除線性，或說增加影像的非線性。

cues.en: Then, we applied a pooling layer to our convolutional layer, so from every single feature map, we created a pooled feature map.
cues.zh: 接著在卷積層後套用池化層，從每張特徵圖產生池化後的特徵圖。

cues.en: And basically, the pooling layer has lots of advantages, the main purpose of the pooling layer is to make sure that we have special invariance in our images,
cues.zh: 池化有許多優點，主要目的是讓影像具有空間不變性，

cues.en: so basically, if something tilts, or twists, or is a bit different to the ideal scenario, then we can still pick up that feature.
cues.zh: 也就是即使特徵傾斜、扭轉，或與理想情況略有不同，我們仍能辨識。

cues.en: Plus, pooling significantly reduces the size of our images, and also, pooling helps with avoiding any kind of overfitting of our data
cues.zh: 池化還能大幅縮小影像，也有助於避免資料的過度擬合，

cues.en: or of our model to the data, because it just simply gets rid of a lot of that data.
cues.zh: 也就是避免模型過度擬合資料，因為它直接移除了大量資料。

cues.en: But at the same time, pooling preserves the main features that we're after, just because the way it's structured, and the pooling we used was max pooling.
cues.zh: 同時，池化的結構也讓我們保留想要的主要特徵。這裡用的是最大池化。

cues.en: Then, we flattened all of the pooled images into one along a vector or column of all of these values, and we input that into an artificial neural network,
cues.zh: 接著把池化後的所有影像，攤平成一個長向量或直行，再輸入人工神經網路。

cues.en: and that was step three flattening, and step four is the fully connected artificial neural network, where all of these features are processed through the network, and then we have this final layer,
cues.zh: 這就是第三步攤平。第四步是全連接人工神經網路，所有特徵在網路中經過處理，最後來到

cues.en: final fully connected layer, which performs the voting towards the classes that we're after, and then, all of this is trained
cues.zh: 最後的全連接層，對我們要辨識的類別投票。整個網路則透過

cues.en: through a forward propagation and backpropagation process, and lots of lots of iterations, and epochs, and in the end, we have a very well defined neural network.
cues.zh: 前向傳播和反向傳播，經過大量迭代與訓練週期，最後形成完善的神經網路。

cues.en: And another important thing is, not only the weights are trained in the artificial neural network part, but also, the feature detectors are trained
cues.zh: 另一個重點是，不只人工神經網路部分的權重會訓練，特徵偵測器也會訓練，

cues.en: and adjusted in that same in gradient descent process, and that allows us to come up with the best feature maps, and in the end, we get a fully trained convolutional neural network,
cues.zh: 並在同樣的梯度下降過程中調整，讓我們得到最佳特徵圖，最終形成訓練完成的卷積神經網路，

cues.en: which can recognize images and classify them.
cues.zh: 能夠辨識影像並分類。

cues.en: So there we go, that's how convolutional neural networks work, and now you should be totally comfortable with this concept and ready to proceed to the practical applications.
cues.zh: 這就是卷積神經網路的運作方式。現在你應該很熟悉這個概念，可以繼續實際應用了。

cues.en: If you'd like to do some additional reading, then there's a great blog by Adit Deshpande from 2016,
cues.zh: 如果想延伸閱讀，有篇 Adit Deshpande 在 2016 年寫的很棒的部落格文章，

cues.en: you can see the link over there at the bottom.
cues.zh: 連結就在下方。

cues.en: So the blog is called "The 9 Deep Learning Papers You Need to Know "About Understanding CNNs Part 3."
cues.zh: 文章叫作 The 9 Deep Learning Papers You Need to Know About，屬於 Understanding CNNs 的第三部分。

cues.en: And this blog actually gives you a short overview of nine different CNNs that have been created by people like Yann LeCun and others, which you can then go ahead and study further.
cues.zh: 它簡要介紹 Yann LeCun 等人建立的九種不同 CNN，讓你可以進一步研究。

cues.en: So there will be a lot of new things that will be totally new to you and that you will have to get your head around, but just keep this blog in mind
cues.zh: 當中有許多全新內容，需要花時間理解。不過先記住這篇文章，

cues.en: or these nine papers in mind, and even if you're not ready to go through them right now, maybe after the practical tutorials, maybe after you do some additional training
cues.zh: 或這九篇論文。即使現在還沒準備好閱讀，也可以等實作教學結束，或進一步學習

cues.en: in the space of Deep Learning, slowly, you can then reference these works, and ideally, I think you will get a lot of value through looking through other people's neural networks
cues.zh: 深度學習之後，再慢慢參考。我認為，研究其他人的神經網路，

cues.en: and how they structured their convolutional nets, and that'll help you understand what are the best practices and why people did certain things in a certain way, and that will help you with your architecture
cues.zh: 看看他們如何建構卷積網路，會很有幫助。你能了解最佳實務，以及為何採取某些做法，進而幫助自己設計

cues.en: of neural networks.
cues.zh: 神經網路架構。

cues.en: Because neural networks and convolutional neural networks are not an exception, they are like an architecture challenge.
cues.zh: 因為神經網路就像架構設計挑戰，卷積神經網路也不例外。

cues.en: You have to come up with a idea, and then structure it, and then adjust it and tweak it to get the best possible design and the best possible and optimal performance.
cues.zh: 必須先有想法，再建構、調整和微調，得到最好的設計，以及最佳效能。

cues.en: So there we go, that's us for today.
cues.zh: 今天就到這裡。

cues.en: I hope you enjoy today's tutorial and this whole section, and I look forward to seeing you next time.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡今天的教學和整個章節，期待下次與你見面。

cues.en: Until then, enjoy Deep Learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
